title: Crash in [@ mozilla::net::nsHttpChannel::ContinueProcessResponse1] and ContinueProcessResponse3 on null mAuthProvider
body:
Crash report: https://crash-stats.mozilla.org/report/index/66dc482c-970b-4280-b6e4-f33400240719

Reason: ```EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION_READ```

Top 10 frames:
```
0  xul.dll  mozilla::net::nsHttpChannel::ContinueProcessResponse1()  netwerk/protocol/http/nsHttpChannel.cpp:2393
1  xul.dll  mozilla::net::nsHttpChannel::ProcessResponse()  netwerk/protocol/http/nsHttpChannel.cpp:2318
1  xul.dll  mozilla::net::nsHttpChannel::OnStartRequest(nsIRequest*)  netwerk/protocol/http/nsHttpChannel.cpp:7560
2  xul.dll  nsInputStreamPump::OnStateStart()  netwerk/base/nsInputStreamPump.cpp:504
2  xul.dll  nsInputStreamPump::OnInputStreamReady(nsIAsyncInputStream*)  netwerk/base/nsInputStreamPump.cpp:409
3  xul.dll  CallbackHolder::CallbackHolder::<lambda_1>:<nick>()() const  xpcom/io/nsPipe3.cpp:86
3  xul.dll  NS_NewCancelableRunnableFunction<`lambda at /builds/worker/checkouts/gecko/xp...  xpcom/threads/nsThreadUtils.h:636
4  xul.dll  mozilla::RunnableTask::Run()  xpcom/threads/TaskController.cpp:580
4  xul.dll  mozilla::TaskController::DoExecuteNextTaskOnlyMainThreadInternal(mozilla::det...  xpcom/threads/TaskController.cpp:907
5  xul.dll  mozilla::TaskController::ExecuteNextTaskOnlyMainThreadInternal(mozilla::detai...  xpcom/threads/TaskController.cpp:730
```

Looks like a new crash signature on release, found by the crash spike detector. There's a similar crash with the signature mozilla::net::nsHttpChannel::ContinueProcessResponse3 which I will file separately though it might be the same issue.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: These are crashes on null.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Looking at a half dozen reports, the crash is on this line: `rv = mAuthProvider->CheckForSuperfluousAuth();` so maybe `mAuthProvider` is null?

comments.author: reporter

comments.author: participant1
reporter
comments.body:
Oh, interesting. From another crash report I found this comment:
```
1. input proxy authentication
2. click remember proxy authentication information
3. enable do not prompt proxy authentication if saved
4. next time open firefix it crash
```
Also another crash has the comment "version 128 crashes when a proxy is configured".

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
We also used this file for proxy settings. 

Right now when I remove comment in mozilla.cfg and restart Firefox twice then it will starts crashing again.

Firefox will download one file - `config.pac` (51kb) from "Script for automatic configuration" in Windows "Internet Settings" and then crash.

But I have no idea why it started crashing now. Missing file is gone for a long time, our admins support only Chrome and Edge.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Looking at the Firefox release notes, I see "Firefox now proxies DNS by default when using SOCKS v5", which looks like it is bug 1741375. Maybe something new getting set over a proxy is causing this issue?

I looked over code related to mAuthProvider and I don't see any recent changes. It looks like it will [always be set to a non-null value in nsHttpChannel::BeginConnect()](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-release/rev/c996b7e06b0bdf1ae6b4e2f2ece6b98504d6dd98/netwerk/protocol/http/nsHttpChannel.cpp#6679) and it [can be set to null in nsHttpChannel::ContinueProcessResponse1()](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-release/rev/c996b7e06b0bdf1ae6b4e2f2ece6b98504d6dd98/netwerk/protocol/http/nsHttpChannel.cpp#2408) if `httpStatus` is not either 401 or 407. That's AFTER the point where we are crashing in ContinueProcessResponse1, but maybe it can get called multiple times?

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: This may be resolved by the pref flip in bug 1908115 per #necko.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: @participant1, can you see if setting the `network.auth.use_redirect_for_retries` pref to false fixes the crashes for you?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
I had that option `false`.

I've created new report with option set to `false`: 3530d9e0-be3f-4a11-a143-ce0940240722
And I tried to set it to `true` 754f3d8b-c383-4900-9c92-c2ffa0240722 but after reporting crash I noticed that option is set to false again.

Firefox is set to "Use system Proxy configuration" (this is forced in Autoconfig file too). Only difference between working Firefox and crashing one is including
```js
lockPref("autoadmin.global_config_url", "http://internal-server/invalid-url/firefox.js");
```
in `mozilla.cfg` Autoconfig file.
